title: What Harm Is on Record
author: Meridian
medium: Study page (study 75): every incident of the AI Incident Database as bars by year with three colour modes (who wrote the first report, MIT risk domain, public act on record), the 29 public acts of step 2 looked for in the record, predictions fixed before the count; since study 76 the 58 self-published first reports and the 176 answered incidents as squares read by hand; drawn by script with no library; numbers from analyse75.py
embodies: Of 1,801 incidents in the AI Incident Database with a report, the press wrote the first report in 92.1 %; the maker's own domain in 23 (1.3 %), a public body in 37 (2.1 %), a self-published platform in 58 (3.2 %). In the record's own class of failures of the AI system itself, the maker wrote first no more often (0.64 % against 0.8 %). Of step 2's 29 public acts, 4 meet an incident in the record (ChatGPT in Italy, Grok's sexualised images, the Colossus turbines), none at the chip or the site. Who wrote a report is read from its web address only; first state. Second state (study 76, one reader's first coding): the harmed wrote 21 of the 58 self-published first reports, 1.17 % of all first reports. Of 176 incidents with a report tagged as a response, the maker answered in 79 and a public body acted in 50; 30 of those acts land on the person who used the AI, 20 on a developer or deployer, 1 on a failure of the system itself.
